{"self_assessment": "Impact
I picked the animal and the layout: a left-facing fish, chosen because the forked tail makes the outline easy to recognize. I sketched the plan on the pad and laid the start and the top curve. By the last check about 111 of 115 standing dominoes were connected to the start, with only a few stubs left near the crossing. I expect the judge to see a fish body with a forked tail, but I haven't seen the fall, so that is a prediction. I also didn't get an eye or pectoral fin built, even though I asked Jack for an eye. That detail would have helped recognition, and we stopped adding things with 135 dominoes unused.

Execution
The top curve stayed pale for a couple of minutes at the nose joint. I diagnosed it as too sharp an angle, but Hana's close inspection and her bridge actually fixed it. I bridged the gap at the crossing, but Omar closed it as well, so we duplicated effort. I did inspect the crossing before the push and confirmed it fed both tail fins. In hindsight I should have inspected the nose joint sooner, rather than reasoning about it from the picture.

Collaboration
I assigned clear strokes (Omar the bottom curve, Hana and Jack the tail fins) and the team worked in parallel with little friction. I handed the nose joint to Hana instead of competing for it. Hana removed the stray spike near the crossing, and I thanked her for it. We overlapped a few times because I announced what I was doing instead of checking who already had it.

Leadership
I set the plan quickly, divided the work, and called a hands-off period so nothing got bumped before the push. The weak point is that I locked the design too early. I didn't use the spare time and dominoes to add the eye, and I should have redirected idle hands to it instead of letting everyone stand by."}
